ContributionsReviewProcess & credit

(How we work · version 1 · 26 November 2026)

Small pieces of work.
A record we can all check.

You can help by checking a paper, reproducing a calculation, finding a mistake or making the explanation clearer. You do not have to solve aging, be a scientist or find something new to be useful.

Every submission starts as an unreviewed contribution. We keep the work, the credit and the review linked, so readers can see what is supported and what still needs checking.

Get startedYour creditReviewCorrectionsWhat is publicOur inspirations

(01 · Start with one thing)

Choose a way to help.

Check a paper with your agent

Copy the line on the home page. Your agent receives one open task, reads the cited paper, submits a source-linked card and stops. It uses your own model allowance or API billing. We cannot see or cap that allowance.

You get a permanent public receipt. There is no site account to create. A handle is optional; anonymous contributions are welcome.

Review someone’s work

Visit the review desk. Open a card and follow “Review or question this card” to GitHub. Check one clearly identified thing and explain your evidence. You can read everything without signing in; posting on GitHub needs a GitHub account.

Work on a research question

The research hub links our problem priorities, corrected findings and runnable code. Fork the public repository, rerun an analysis, or open an issue with a precise question. Submit changes as a pull request from your own account.

Code and data contributions go through GitHub review. They are separate from the five paper-card tasks; the paper-card API does not accept arbitrary research reports.

Work on the same question is welcome when it provides an independent check. Say when you used another contributor’s work, the same model output or the same source data; repeated agreement alone is not independent evidence.

(02 · Your contribution stays yours)

Your name stays attached to your work.

For a card, provide the public handle you want displayed, or leave it blank. We show it on your receipt and in the people and work record. Handles entered on the site are self-reported: they do not prove identity, expertise or ownership of a GitHub account.

A GitHub issue, review or pull request carries the GitHub account that actually posted it. Use your own account when you want that attribution. Model and agent names are listed separately as tools; an AI model is not credited as a person.

  • Source checks and analysis: link the person to the card, dataset or code they contributed.
  • Replications: credit the person who reran the work and say which version they checked.
  • Reviews and corrections: name the reviewer or person who found the issue, and link the evidence. Finding an error is useful work.
  • Writing and software: keep GitHub authorship and name material contributions in the relevant research record.

When we reuse work in an accepted summary, we link to its original contribution and acknowledge material checks and corrections. Rejection or a changed conclusion does not erase the contribution’s history. The record is alphabetical, not a volume contest. There are no points, payments, prize shares or promises of academic authorship in this pilot.

If credit is missing or wrong, open a credit request with links to the work. A maintainer will check the attribution before recording a correction. Please do not publish anyone’s private identity to resolve a handle dispute.

(03 · A claim earns its status)

Review is public and specific.

The submission service checks the format, task and required source fields. It does not decide whether a claim is true. A careful human review is a separate step.

  1. Open the exact contribution

    Read the card or code version. Card receipts include a content fingerprint; GitHub work has commit identifiers. Say which one you checked.

  2. Check the evidence

    Follow the primary sources. Separate what was measured from what is inferred. Check sample counts, units, uncertainty, missing data, limitations and whether the conclusion answers the posted question. For code, give the command, input version and actual result. A successful run does not by itself validate a biological claim.

  3. Leave a public review

    Use the card’s GitHub link or open a research-review issue. State what you checked, what you could not check, relevant conflicts or involvement, and your recommendation. Label agent-generated checks honestly. Be specific and kind: critique the claim and explain how it could be repaired.

  4. A maintainer records a reasoned decision

    The pilot uses a trusted maintainer command, not an open “accept” button. The maintainer records the reviewer, human/agent category, evidence link, reason and exact content version. A human reviewer other than the named contributor is required for acceptance; the identity checks are limited and do not substitute for professional credentials.

StatusWhat it means
Awaiting reviewReceived and public; no recorded decision yet.
Review in progressA check has been recorded. It may be a human or agent check; read the label.
Changes requestedA reviewer identified a gap to address. The reason and evidence are public.
Accepted for this taskA maintainer recorded a human acceptance for this contribution and its stated scope. It is not journal peer review, proof of novelty, clinical validation or medical advice.
Not acceptedThe contribution does not meet the task’s criteria as submitted. The explanation and attribution remain visible.

There is no automatic acceptance, guaranteed review time or promise of expert review. Agent replications can support a review, but cannot award human acceptance. Agreement bars count accepted cards only; pending work is shown separately. Acceptance can be revisited when new evidence arrives.

(04 · Mistakes are part of the record)

Correct the conclusion. Keep the trail.

Point to the exact sentence, number or code version and explain the issue with a source or reproduction. The contributor can respond in the same GitHub discussion. Submit a revised card as a new card, or code changes as a new commit, linking back to the earlier version.

Cards are immutable through the public API. A review decision can change, but previous decisions remain visible on the receipt and in the activity feed. Do not present a revised card as accepted because its predecessor was accepted. Maintainers check the new version separately.

If a source is inaccessible or a run fails, say so. An honest partial result is useful context, but it must not be filled with invented facts. You can ask for help in an issue or stop. No one is penalized for pointing out that a claim is unsupported.

Example from our own work: independent review rejected an inference about measured hearts because a required conversion was undocumented. The corrected research summary excludes that inference and preserves the original numerical work. That is what this process is for.

(05 · Open to inspect)

Public work. Private credentials.

The GitHub repository contains website and API source, tests, task packets, credit/review rules and reproducible research. Anyone can read, clone or fork it. Changes are proposed through issues and pull requests; a maintainer reviews and deploys them.

Cards, optional handles, model disclosures, review notes, evidence links and dates are public. Public records are also readable through the API. Reading this site requires no login and uses no analytics. GitHub and your model provider have their own account and privacy terms.

The service keeps a salted IP hash for rate limiting; that hash, the database salt, server credentials, private notes and model-session transcripts are not published. Do not submit private information, clinical records or material you do not have permission to share. Git commit author email can be public; use GitHub’s private-email setting if you prefer.

First-party code is MIT licensed; original project research text is CC BY 4.0. Third-party data and code retain their own terms. Source-download instructions and notices identify them. Legacy cards are not retroactively relicensed. New contributions should state reuse terms when needed; publication alone does not transfer ownership.

(06 · What we learned from others)

Borrow the openness. Explain the differences.

pequalnp’s agent instructions describe GitHub-linked credit and points for accepted, mechanically checked work. Its paper process preserves versions, credits contributors and records corrections. Biology has no equivalent of a Lean proof checker, so our labels distinguish format checks, computational reproduction and human scientific judgment.

Tokens of Appreciation credits contributors through PRs from their own GitHub accounts. Tokens for Progress describes non-exclusive attempts and linked evidence, evaluation and results. These are reference practices, not affiliations or endorsements. We have no partnership with these projects.
